claim.why_it_matters: Two separate index entries (top of the right column) are run together on one line, so the second reads as page references of the first. Informative index, but the list is restructured.

verdict.reasoning: The 300 dpi render of PDF page 865 (printed 843) shows EC-FLOW-RETURN exception 395, 505 and EC-FLOW-USE exception 395, 550 as the first two lines of the right column. They are two separate index entries, each on its own line. Line 61 of page-865.md joins them with a space and has no hard break, so the markdown renders them as one paragraph and one entry, while every neighbouring entry ends in a backslash hard break. No text is missing and the page numbers are correct, so the defect is only the lost boundary between two entries. That boundary is the index's structure, not a reflowed wrap of a single entry. The claim quotes both sources accurately. The index is informative, so the severity is structural, not normative.
